parsed.why: Top-tier protective division: statewide gender-identity protections, constitutional amendment, hate-crime coverage, gender-neutral bathrooms, shield statutes. National border, federal-facility and custody regime still binds, capping the score well below Low Risk.

Low-risk tier, no facility restriction, court-protected bathroom access, hate-crime enhancement, X markers. Lacks the shield/constitutional layers of peers and shows institutional capitulation on sports; parent border and federal rules still apply.

Moderate tier: no adult facility or care ban, but no statewide nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage — visitors lack recourse for service denial or bias violence. Thin tier-3 exposure near the parent mean.

Most-protective tier: public-accommodations ban reaching hotels and services, hate-crime penalties since 1999, panic-defence repeal, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, shield laws. National document and federal-facility regime prevents a higher score.

Worst-tier division adding a statewide biological-sex facility ban with a private cause of action — a tier-1 universal exposure — plus no nondiscrimination, no state hate-crime law, sports and youth-care bans; materially below parent.
